title: v0.42 is changing pane arrangement strategies on mouse movement
body:
## Issue description

Zellij v0.42.0 is changing arrangement strategies on mouse movement.
I have a single line config, `pane_frames false`.

## Minimal reproduction

minimal setup to reproduce it: open a second pane and move the mouse over your terminal.

## Other relevant information

I don't know if it's relevant, but that's on Windows 11 WSL with Ubuntu using Microsoft Terminal.

comments.body:
So, I'm not sure why exactly this happens but from a casual glance (and without having full access to the app) it seems like the windows terminal implementation of Mouse Any-Event tracking is slightly different than the ones I've encountered in other terminals (and in the xterm spec) when implementing this protocol. I didn't see anything in this dump that would cause the issue, but I'm assuming it's something in this neighborhood.

I'm going to release a patch version in the next few days that will allow disabling just mouse motion detection in the config, which should mitigate this issue while still maintaining the bulk of mouse support.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
After some investigation (and learning how to read Rust), I think I found the issue.
Looking at the [relevant xterm documentation](https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h2-Mouse-Tracking) reveals that the structure of mouse reports is this:
`CSI < B ; Px ; Py M` for button pressed
`CSI < B ; Px ; Py m` for button released
`Px` and `Py` are coordinates and `B` is button+modifiers
To make a long story short B=3 means no buttons and mouse movements add 32 to that, so for mouse movements with no button presses B=35.

Some quick tests revealed Windows Terminal uses `CSI < 35 ; Px ; Py m` to report mouse moves with no buttons while WezTerm and xterm (and probably all the others) use `CSI < 35 ; Px ; Py M`.

Now, from what I could understand, `termwiz` only handles the `M` case when B=35 (see [here](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/7053748e4d899e7fc5e202d6f903b052fc78e759/termwiz/src/escape/csi.rs#L2222)).
